notes.summary: An analogy question gives a pair with a hidden relationship and asks you to find another pair with the same relationship. SSC asks 2–3 analogy questions in Tier 1 (word, number and letter types).

concepts.title: Find the rule first
concepts.body: Look at the first pair and say the link in one short sentence: "A works in B", "B is the square of A", "each letter moves +1". Then apply the same sentence to the second pair.

concepts.title: Common number rules
concepts.body: Square (n²), cube (n³), n² ± n, n³ ± 1, ×2 +1, sum of digits. Check the rule on the given pair before using it.

concepts.title: Common letter rules
concepts.body: Each letter moves forward/backward by a fixed number, or the shift grows (+1, +2, +3). Use the position table: A=1 … Z=26. Opposite letter pairs add to 27 (A–Z, B–Y).

varieties.name: Word analogy
varieties.how: State the link (worker–place, tool–use, part–whole, product–raw material) and apply it.

steps: A pen is used to write.
A knife is used to cut.

varieties.name: Number analogy
varieties.how: Test squares, cubes and n³ ± n on the first pair.

varieties.name: Letter analogy
varieties.how: Write letter positions and find the shift for each letter.

tips: Check your rule on the first pair before applying it; many wrong options fit a "nearly right" rule.
For letters, write positions (A=1 … Z=26) under each letter: shifts become obvious.
For number pairs, try n², n³, n² + 1, n³ + n in that order.
traps: Do not reverse the order of the pair: Doctor : Hospital is not the same as Hospital : Doctor.
In letter analogies the shift may be different for each letter (+1, +2, +3).

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.solution:
A doctor works in a hospital.
A teacher works in a school.
So the answer is School.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?).
4 : 16 :: 7 : ?
questions.solution:
Rule: second number = square of the first.
4² = 16.
7² = 49.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first.
ACE : BDF :: GIK : ?
questions.solution:
A→B, C→D, E→F: each letter +1.
G+1 = H, I+1 = J, K+1 = L.
Answer: HJL.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?).
3 : 28 :: 5 : ?
In a certain way, CAT is related to DCW. In the same way, DOG is related to:
questions.solution:
C→D (+1), A→C (+2), T→W (+3).
Apply +1, +2, +3 to DOG:
D+1 = E, O+2 = Q, G+3 = J.
Answer: EQJ.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?).
6 : 222 :: 8 : ?

flashcards.back: Say the relation of the first pair in one sentence, test it, then apply it to the second pair.

flashcards.front: Letter positions: E, J, O, T, Y

flashcards.back: Positions of a letter and its opposite add to 27 (A–Z, M–N).
